messages:
matt: Heads up — trying to repro a perf regression in KV cache. What's a good minimal nsys command for a short targeted run? File sizes are killing me.

sara: Use NVTX markers to bracket the region. Then capture only that range (nsys has capture-range=nvtx), so you don't record everything. Saves huge space.

oliver: Also include OS runtime tracing. I usually do --trace=cuda,nvtx,osrt so kernels + NVTX + OS events show up on the timeline. Keep the capture duration short (5-15s) to limit .qdrep size.

jin: Example I run locally:
```
nsys profile --output=kv_probe \
  --trace=cuda,nvtx,osrt \
  --capture-range=nvtx:KV_RUN_BEGIN:KV_RUN_END \
  --duration=12s \
  --sample-interval=20ms \
  --force-overwrite -- my_bench --mode=kv --iter=100
```
This uses NVTX markers around the exact workload, sets a modest sample interval, and forces overwrite so CI runs don't pile up.

sara: If you only need kernel timings and NVTX context, try `--sample=none` to disable callstack sampling. That drops overhead a lot and keeps files small.

matt: How do you tune sampling to still get hotspots but avoid giant captures?

oliver: Tradeoff: increase --sample-interval (less frequent samples) or use `--sample=cpu` only. If kernel durations are long, coarse sampling still catches hotspots. If kernels are short and many, bracket tightly with NVTX.

perf-bot: Automated tip: to extract kernel-level tables without opening UI, run `nsys stats -i kv_probe.qdrep --report=summary` or export CSVs with `nsys export`. Useful for grep/CI checks.

jin: Pro tip: don't set CUDA_LAUNCH_BLOCKING=1 for perf runs unless debugging a race — it serializes and changes timing. For KV batching traces, keep async behavior.

sara: If you see scheduling gaps, `osrt` events help correlate context switches/CPU blocking to kernel gaps. Also annotate hot code paths with NVTX names that include batch size / seq len so traces are self-describing.

matt: OK will try a 12s NVTX-bracketed run with sample=none first, then a longer sample-interval run if I need hotspots. I'll attach qdrep if I hit something weird.

oliver: :thumbsup:

matt: (followup later) ran bracketed capture, file was ~9MB and the kernel timeline shows repeated tiny kernels around KV eviction. Posting when I have a screenshot.
